adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the mapping that builds reference fields changes `credentialId` from `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` (around the shown line ~170). This demonstrably drops `credentialId` for all non-calendar results (e.g., video/conferencing integrations) where `isCalendarType` is false, even though `result.credentialId` may be present. That is a behavior change introduced by the diff and can break later operations that rely on stored `credentialId` to locate the correct integration credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without `?.` after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so any booking with no destination calendar throws when location is Google Meet instead of falling back to Cal Video (P1, conf 75)

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` ignores the passed credentialId, so when EventManager fans out over collective hosts each teammate's Office365 credential POSTs to `/me/calendars/<main host externalId>/events`, failing or hitting the wrong calendar (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept `(event, credentialId)` and updates Google to select the destination calendar matching that `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). However, `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` still has `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and now explicitly uses only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then builds `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`). Separately, `handleNewBooking.ts` appends additional collective hosts’ destination calendars to `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` fans out over `event.destinationCalendar`, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination. Since Office365 ignores `credentialId` (and any per-destination selection) and always uses the first destination calendar, collective host credentials can POST to the main host’s calendar externalId, hitting the wrong calendar or failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark createEvent/createAttendees always use destinationCalendar[0].externalId regardless of which credential is calling, so non-primary collective hosts write to the organizer's calendar id with their own token (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `createEvent` and `createAttendees` were changed to destructure only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and then use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` as the calendarId. Meanwhile, the diff changes the system to support multiple `destinationCalendar` entries (`DestinationCalendar[]`) and to create events per credential (e.g., `CalendarManager.createEvent` now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops over `event.destinationCalendar`). Unlike the Google implementation, Lark does not select the calendar based on the calling credential; it will always use index 0. This can cause non-primary/secondary collective hosts to attempt to write using their own credential/token but targeting the organizer’s calendar externalId (destinationCalendar[0]), which is incorrect behavior and can lead to wrong-calendar writes or failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — CalDAV/iCal base service filters by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, so a second host's credential finds zero matching calendars and silently creates nothing (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` the CalDAV/iCal base service now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then filters calendars by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (only the first destination calendar). With the diff changing `destinationCalendar` to an array and `handleNewBooking` appending additional team destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), creating events for a non-first destination/credential can result in `calendars.filter(...)` returning an empty list for that credential, leading to `Promise.all([])` and no event being created (effectively silently doing nothing). This is consistent with the finding and is directly verifiable from the filter logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — destinationCalendar is `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` at :1078 is a no-op and all collective teammates' calendars are dropped (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (see the ternary at ~1060). Later, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` (~1078). If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, so any `teamDestinationCalendars` gathered from other users are never added. This matches the finding that collective teammates’ destination calendars can be dropped in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — Booking persists only `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, and cancel/reschedule/deleteCredential rebuild `[booking.destinationCalendar]`, so the multi-host destination list is lost after creation (data model does not carry the new array shape) (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, explicitly appends additional host destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` in `handleNewBooking.ts`). However, when persisting the booking it only connects a single destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so any additional destination calendars added to the event are not stored on the Booking record. Subsequent code paths shown in the diff rebuild event destination calendars from the persisted singular `booking.destinationCalendar`/`user.destinationCalendar` (wrapped into a one-element array), so the extra destinations cannot be recovered from the booking data model after creation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:374 — the no-credentialId `else` branch now runs per destination, calling createEvent on every credential of that integration type for each destination, yielding N destinations x M credentials duplicate external events (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` runs an `else` branch when a destination lacks `credentialId`. That branch filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `c.type === destination.integration` and then calls `createEvent(c, event)` for *each* matching credential. Because this happens inside the `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop, multiple destinations without `credentialId` will repeat the same “create on all credentials of this integration” behavior, producing N(destinations w/o credentialId) × M(credentials of that type) external events. Previously, this “create on all credentials of integration” path ran once for a single `event.destinationCalendar?.integration`, not once per destination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:447 — recurring-cancel branch is inside the per-reference loop yet iterates all `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` x `updatedBookings` using only `references.find(...)` (first ref), producing repeated identical deletes per reference while other hosts' calendar events are never deleted (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, bookingCalendarReference is now an array (filter) and the code loops `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that per-reference loop, the recurring-cancel branch (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) still iterates over *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and over *all* `updatedBookings`, and for each updated booking it deletes only `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (the first matching ref). Because this whole block is executed once per `reference`, it will repeat the same deletions multiple times (duplicated deletes) and it will miss deleting additional calendar references per updated booking beyond the first `find(...)` result.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:343 — `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` loads any credential (including its OAuth `key`) by ID with no check that it belongs to a host of this booking/event type, so a destinationCalendar pointing at a foreign credentialId (e.g. eventType.destinationCalendar set by a team admin, or a stale one after membership removal) makes cal.com write events using another user's calendar account (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` (new loop in `createAllCalendarEvents`), when a `destination.credentialId` isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches a credential via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then constructs a `credential` object including `key` and uses it to `createEvent(...)`. The lookup is not scoped (no `userId`/team/org/host check) to ensure the credential belongs to the event’s organizer/hosts. Given that `destinationCalendar` now comes from persisted data (`eventType.destinationCalendar`, `user.destinationCalendar`, and pushed team member destination calendars), a stale or incorrect `credentialId` could cause events to be created using an unrelated credential purely by ID, which is a security/correctness defect exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:516 — the update path does the same unscoped `prisma.credential.findUnique` on `reference.credentialId` and uses the credential to modify events without verifying ownership against the booking's hosts (P1, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, the updated loop over calendar references adds a fallback that fetches a credential directly from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` when it isn’t present in `this.calendarCredentials`, then uses it to call `updateEvent(...)` (and similarly in cancellation code). The diff shows no verification that the fetched credential belongs to the booking’s organizer/hosts (e.g., matching userId/teamId) before using it to modify calendar events. This is a concrete, diff-introduced authorization gap consistent with the finding.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:249 — `log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent)` logs the full CalendarEvent (attendee emails, names, notes, and now every collective host's destinationCalendar/credentialId), and with the new per-host loop this PII goes to logs once per failing host (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` still does `log.error("createEvent failed", JSON.stringify(error), calEvent)` inside the `createEvent` catch block, which logs the full `CalendarEvent` object. In this PR `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` was changed from a single object to an array (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`), and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` was changed to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` and call `createEvent(...)` for each destination/credential. That makes the same full-event (attendees, notes, and now multiple destination calendars/credentialIds) potentially logged repeatedly per failing host/credential, increasing PII exposure. This is a verifiable security/privacy defect grounded in the diff.
